_why: ADR 0125's mutation table, re-derived under scripts/mutate.py.
The record shipped its three mutations as prose. This encodes them so a
reader can re-run the claim rather than trust it -- ADR 0069's whole
point, written after the hand-run harness had been wrong three separate
HOW FAITHFUL THIS IS, SAID PLAINLY
These patches were reconstructed on 2026-08-24 from the record's own
descriptions and the code they describe, NOT from the author's original
diffs, which were never committed. Each row below names the mutation ADR
0125 listed and the exact line in src/web/dashboard.html that implements
the behaviour it describes. If a mutation here is subtly different from
the one the author ran, this file is wrong in a way the ADR's prose is
not -- so the reconstruction is stated rather than implied.
`confidence` measured literature source count and was rendered as a
percentage, so one "0%" meant three different things: the run failed, the
run errored, or the run was perfect and made no literature claim. The fix
renders an em-dash for failure and `n/a` for a correct unsourced run.

mutations.description: the cell forces a percentage again
mutations._note: The defect exactly: an unsourced run renders 0.0% and is indistinguishable from a failure. This is the branch ADR 0125 added; removing it restores the ambiguity the record exists to describe.

Keeps the conditional but collapses the unsourced arm onto the percentage, so a correct run that made no literature claim reports a number it has no basis for. Distinct from M1: the shape survives and only the honest label goes.

The em-dash on the job-failure path becomes '0', which is the original conflation reintroduced at the other end: a failed run reporting a score. The second failure path (the catch block at :725) is left alone on purpose, so this mutation isolates one of the two.
